QUESTIONS.EVALUATION-NOTES: Split data first, fit preprocessing only on training data, then apply it to validation/test data; a seed does not fix leakage.

QUESTIONS.EVALUATION-NOTES: C is true; then A is false and B is false, so exactly one statement is true.

QUESTIONS.EVALUATION-NOTES: A,B,C,D or B,A,C,D; A and B precede C, and C precedes D.

QUESTIONS.QUESTION-PROMPT: A negative-feedback controller reacts too strongly and oscillations grow. Explain how controller gain and delay can affect stability, and name one change that may improve it.
QUESTIONS.EVALUATION-NOTES: Excessive gain and delay can destabilize feedback; reducing gain or delay may help, depending on system dynamics.

QUESTIONS.QUESTION-PROMPT: In a hypothetical world where surface gravitational acceleration is 10 times Earth's, assume atmosphere and aircraft technology otherwise unchanged. Explain qualitatively how takeoff and sustained flight would be affected, and name one limiting assumption.
QUESTIONS.EVALUATION-NOTES: Weight would be much greater, requiring more lift/thrust and making flight harder; exact feasibility depends on aircraft design, atmosphere, and structural limits.

QUESTIONS.QUESTION-PROMPT: In a hypothetical universe, electrons retain their mass but have zero electric charge, while protons remain positively charged and electromagnetic interactions otherwise follow usual charge rules. What major change would this imply for ordinary atoms and chemistry? State a limitation.
QUESTIONS.EVALUATION-NOTES: Electrons would not be electrostatically attracted to nuclei or form ordinary electron-mediated bonds, radically altering familiar chemistry; detailed outcomes depend on the counterfactual physics.

QUESTIONS.QUESTION-PROMPT: In a hypothetical transparent medium, light's phase velocity is half its vacuum value while frequency remains unchanged. What happens to wavelength and photon energy? Do not infer a photosynthesis-efficiency change without additional assumptions.
QUESTIONS.EVALUATION-NOTES: Wavelength halves because wavelength=speed/frequency; photon energy E=hf remains unchanged at fixed frequency. Photosynthesis impact is not determined by these facts alone.

VERSIONING-NOTE: Test prompts and answer keys live here. Scoring criteria are governed by a separately versioned scoring rubric. Do not edit V1 or V1 raw results.

RUN-PROTOCOL.MATCHING: Use the same base model/version, capabilities, sampling parameters, tools, context, and prompt sequence across conditions wherever technically possible; document unavoidable differences.
RUN-PROTOCOL.REPETITIONS: For paired condition comparisons, target at least 5 independent paired runs per model/version and condition, each in fresh category sessions with unchanged settings. If fewer runs are feasible, label the results exploratory pilot data. Stability analyses require at least 5 independent repetitions of the exact same prompt sequence per condition; do not treat questions within one session as independent runs.
RUN-PROTOCOL.FIELD_POLICY: Preserve raw output exactly. The scoring rubric must predeclare which response fields are eligible for substantive credit. Report primary-field completion and any-eligible-field completion separately.
RUN-PROTOCOL.RANDOMIZATION: Randomize condition order and blind evaluators to condition labels where feasible.
RUN-PROTOCOL.MISSINGNESS: Record missing runs and blank answers explicitly. Do not silently convert missing files into zero scores.
RUN-PROTOCOL.SESSION_BOUNDARIES: Present questions within each category in listed order in one continuous conversation so explicit multi-turn items can use prior turns. Start a fresh conversation for each category and each repetition to prevent cross-category carryover. Do not split C4 or R2 into isolated single-question calls.
